There are $N\ge2$ empty boxes $B_1,\ldots,B_N$ in a row and an unlimited supply of pebbles. Given a positive integer $n$, Pic and Ping play a game of darkness. In the first round, Pic distributes $n$ pebbles among the boxes as he wishes. Each subsequent round has two steps: (i) Ping chooses $1\le k\le N-1$ and splits the boxes into groups $B_1,\ldots,B_k$ and $B_{k+1},\ldots,B_N$. (ii) Pic chooses one group, adds one pebble to each box in it, and removes one pebble from each box in the other group. Ping becomes the next team leader if, at the end of some round, a box contains no pebbles. Find the smallest $n$ for which Pic can prevent this.

Let $ABC$ have circumcircle $\Gamma$. Let $\omega_0$ be a circle tangent to chord $AB$ and arc $ACB$. For $i=1,2$, let $\omega_i$ be tangent to $AB$ at $T_i$, to $\omega_0$ at $S_i$, and to arc $ACB$. Suppose $\omega_1\ne\omega_2$. Prove that there is a circle through $S_1,S_2,T_1,T_2$ tangent to $\Gamma$ if and only if $\angle ACB=90^\circ$.

On a flat plane in Camelot, King Arthur builds a labyrinth of $n$ walls, each an infinite straight line. No two walls are parallel and no three meet at one point. Merlin paints one side of each wall entirely red and the other entirely blue. At each intersection of two walls, a two-way door connects the diagonally opposite corners at which sides of different colours meet. Morgana places knights in the labyrinth. They can walk through doors but cannot walk through walls. Find the largest $k$ such that, regardless of the labyrinth and its colouring, Morgana can place $k$ knights so that no two can ever meet.

Consider functions $f:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$ satisfying $$f(f(x+y)+y)=f(f(x)+y)$$ for all integers $x,y$. Call an integer $v$ $f$-rare if $X_v=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid f(x)=v\}$ is finite and non-empty. Prove that no such function can have more than one $f$-rare integer.

Let $N\ge2$ be an integer and $u_1,u_2,\ldots,u_{2019}$ be real numbers satisfying $$u_1+\cdots+u_N=0\qquad\text{and}\qquad u_1^2+\cdots+u_N^2=1.$$ Let $a=\min\{u_1,\ldots,u_N\}$ and $b=\max\{u_1,\ldots,u_N\}$. Prove that $ab\le-1/N$.

Call a set $S$ of integers rootiful if, for every positive integer $n$ and all integers $a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_n\in S$, all integer roots of $a_0+a_1x+\cdots+a_nx^n$ also belong to $S$. Find all rootiful sets containing every number of the form $2^a-2^b$ for positive integers $a\ge b$.

Let $L$ be the set of all lines in the plane, and let $f$ assign to each line $\ell\in L$ a point $f(\ell)$ on $\ell$. Suppose that for every point $X$ and any three lines $\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3$ through $X$, the points $f(\ell_1),f(\ell_2),f(\ell_3),X$ lie on a circle. Prove that there is a unique point $P$ such that $f(\ell)=P$ for every line $\ell$ through $P$.

For a positive integer $n$, consider a square cake divided into $n\times n$ pieces, with at most one strawberry on each piece. Call the cake delicious if both diagonals are fully occupied and each row and column has an odd number of strawberries. Find all positive integers $n$ for which a delicious cake exists with exactly $\lceil n^2/2\rceil$ strawberries.
Prove that for all positive integers $m,n$, $$\lfloor m\sqrt2\rfloor\,\lfloor n\sqrt7\rfloor<\lfloor mn\sqrt{14}\rfloor.$$

Let $P$ be on the circumcircle of an acute triangle $ABC$. Let $D,E,F$ be the reflections of $P$ in the perpendicular bisectors of the altitudes of $ABC$ parallel to $BC,CA,AB$, respectively. Let $\omega_A,\omega_B,\omega_C$ be the circumcircles of $ADP,BEP,CFP$, respectively. Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of the triangle formed by the perpendicular bisectors of $AD,BE,CF$. Show that $\omega_A,\omega_B,\omega_C,\omega$ have a common point.

Given a positive integer $k$, show that there is a prime $p$ for which one can choose distinct integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{k+3}\in\{1,2,\ldots,p-1\}$ such that $p\mid a_i a_{i+1}a_{i+2}a_{i+3}-i$ for all $i=1,2,\ldots,k$.
Let $a,b,c,d$ be positive real numbers satisfying $(a+c)(b+d)=ac+bd$. Find the smallest possible value of $$S=\frac ab+\frac bc+\frac cd+\frac da.$$

Let $p$ be an odd prime and $N=(p^3-p)/4-1$. Colour the numbers $1,2,\ldots,N$ arbitrarily red or blue. For $1\le n\le N$, let $r(n)$ be the fraction of numbers in $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ that are red. Prove that there is an $a\in\{1,2,\ldots,p-1\}$ such that $r(n)\ne a/p$ for all $n=1,2,\ldots,N$.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $\angle ABC>90^\circ$, $\angle CDA>90^\circ$ and $\angle DAB=\angle BCD$. Let $E,F$ be the reflections of $A$ in $BC,CD$, respectively. Suppose segments $AE,AF$ meet line $BD$ at $K,L$, respectively. Prove that the circumcircles of $BEK,DFL$ are tangent to each other.

For an odd prime $p$ and an integer $n$, let $d_p(n)\in\{0,1,\ldots,p-1\}$ be the remainder of $n$ modulo $p$. Call $(a_0,a_1,\ldots)$ a $p$-sequence if $a_0$ is a positive integer coprime to $p$ and $a_{n+1}=a_n+d_p(a_n)$ for $n\ge0$. (a) Are there infinitely many primes $p$ for which there are $p$-sequences $(a_n)$ and $(b_n)$ such that $a_n>b_n$ for infinitely many $n$ and $b_n>a_n$ for infinitely many $n$? (b) Are there infinitely many primes $p$ for which there are $p$-sequences $(a_n)$ and $(b_n)$ with $a_0<b_0$ but $a_n>b_n$ for all $n\ge1$?

Consider a rectangular table with finitely many rows and columns and a real number $a(r,c)$ in row $r$, column $c$. A pair $(R,C)$, with $R$ a set of rows and $C$ a set of columns, is a saddle pair if: (i) for every row $r\prime$, some $r\in R$ satisfies $a(r,c)\ge a(r\prime,c)$ for all $c\in C$; (ii) for every column $c\prime$, some $c\in C$ satisfies $a(r,c)\le a(r,c\prime)$ for all $r\in R$. A saddle pair is minimal if every saddle pair $(R\prime,C\prime)$ with $R\prime\subseteq R$ and $C\prime\subseteq C$ satisfies $R\prime=R$ and $C\prime=C$. Prove that any two minimal pairs contain the same number of rows.
Let $n$ be a positive integer and $N=2^n$. Determine the smallest real number $a_n$ such that, for every real number $x$, $$\sqrt[N]{\frac{x^{2N}+1}{2}}\le a_n(x-1)^2+x.$$

A plane contains $n\ge6$ pairwise disjoint disks $D_1,\ldots,D_n$ with radii $R_1\ge\cdots\ge R_n$. Choose $P_i$ in $D_i$ for each $i$. For any point $O$ in the plane, prove that $$OP_1+\cdots+OP_n\ge R_6+R_7+\cdots+R_n.$$ A disk includes its boundary.

Determine all functions on the positive integers with non-negative integer values satisfying: (i) $f(n)\ne0$ for at least one $n$; (ii) $f(xy)=f(x)+f(y)$ for every positive integers $x,y$; (iii) there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $f(k)=f(n-k)$ for all positive integers $k<n$.

For each prime $p$, the kingdom of $p$-Landia has $p$ islands numbered $1,2,\ldots,p$. Two distinct islands numbered $n,m$ are joined by a bridge if and only if $p\mid(n^2-m+1)(m^2-n+1)$. Bridges may pass over each other but cannot cross. Prove that for infinitely many primes $p$, two islands are not connected by a chain of bridges.

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral with no two sides parallel. Points $K,L,M,N$ lie on $AB,BC,CD,DA$, respectively, such that $KLMN$ is a rhombus with $KL\parallel AC$, $LM\parallel BD$. Let $\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3,\omega_4$ be the incircles of $ANK,BKL,CLM,DMN$, respectively. Prove that the two internal common tangents to $\omega_1,\omega_3$ and the two internal common tangents to $\omega_2,\omega_4$ are concurrent. An internal common tangent intersects the segment joining the centres of the circles.
Determine all functions $f:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$ satisfying $$f^{a^2+b^2}(a+b)=af(a)+bf(b)$$ for all integers $a,b$. Here $f^n$ denotes iteration: $f^0(x)=x$ and $f^{n+1}(x)=f(f^n(x))$ for $n\ge0$.

In a regular $100$-gon, $41$ vertices are black and the remaining $59$ white. Prove that there exist $24$ pairwise disjoint convex quadrilaterals $Q_1,\ldots,Q_{24}$ whose corners are vertices of the polygon, each with three corners of one colour and one corner of the other colour.

Let $A$ consist of all natural numbers $n$ for which there are $k\in\mathbb N$ and $a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}\in\{1,2,\ldots,9\}$ with $a_0\ge a_1\ge\cdots\ge a_{k-1}$ and $n=a_0+a_1 10+\cdots+a_{k-1}10^{k-1}$. Let $B$ consist of all natural numbers $m$ for which there are $\ell\in\mathbb N$ and $b_0,\ldots,b_{\ell-1}\in\{1,2,\ldots,9\}$ with $b_0\le b_1\le\cdots\le b_{\ell-1}$ and $m=b_0+b_1 10+\cdots+b_{\ell-1}10^{\ell-1}$. (a) Are there infinitely many $n\in A$ with $n^2-3\in A$? (b) Are there infinitely many $m\in B$ with $m^2-3\in B$?

A magician announces a positive integer $n$ and $2n$ real numbers $x_1<x_2<\cdots<x_{2n}$. An audience member secretly chooses a real polynomial $P(x)$ of degree $n$, computes $P(x_1),\ldots,P(x_{2n})$ and writes these values on the board in non-decreasing order. The magician then announces the secret polynomial. Can she find a strategy to perform this trick?

Let $A$ be the set of polynomials in $x,y,z$ with integer coefficients. Let $B$ be the subset expressible as $$(x+y+z)P(x,y,z)+(xy+yz+zx)Q(x,y,z)+xyzR(x,y,z)$$ with $P,Q,R\in A$. Find the smallest non-negative integer $n$ such that $x^i y^j z^k\in B$ for all non-negative integers $i,j,k$ with $i+j+k\ge n$.

The Fibonacci numbers are defined by $F_0=0$, $F_1=1$, $F_{n+1}=F_n+F_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$. Given $n\ge2$, determine the smallest size of a set $S$ of integers such that, for every $k=2,3,\ldots,n$, there exist $x,y\in S$ with $x-y=F_k$.

Let $I,I_A$ be the incentre and the $A$-excentre of an acute triangle $ABC$ with $AB<AC$. Let the incircle touch $BC$ at $D$. Line $AD$ meets $BI_A,CI_A$ at $E,F$, respectively. Prove that the circumcircles of $AID,I_AEF$ are tangent to each other.
